claims.text: Molecular dynamics simulations using multi-element EAM-type potentials can accurately capture the size-dependent thermal response of FeCuCrCoNi high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles.
Smaller FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles have lower melting temperatures than larger FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles.
The synthesized FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticles have a homogeneous distribution of constituent elements.
Controlled heating rates ensure thermal equilibrium and reliable melting-point estimates in these simulations.
Decreasing nanoparticle size increases the surface-to-volume ratio.
A higher surface-to-volume ratio increases the proportion of undercoordinated atoms.
Smaller nanoparticles have a higher fraction of surface atoms.
Surface atoms in these nanoparticles have lower cohesive energies.
The lower cohesive energies of surface atoms cause atomic mobility and melting to begin at lower temperatures.
As FeCuCrCoNi nanoparticle size decreases, the melting transition range broadens.
Lower melting temperatures and broader melting transitions indicate reduced thermal stability.
The predictive accuracy of the simulations is limited by the accuracy of the interatomic potentials.
The predictive accuracy of the simulations is limited by the timescales accessible to molecular dynamics.
